text:
Sean Strickland has offered his latest scathing assessment of the Trump administration after being denied access to the UFC White House event

Recently crowned UFC Middleweight Champion Sean Strickland has continued his attack on the Trump administration in the wake of his UFC White House ban by taking aim at its "fascist views on speech".

Strickland, 35, last week revealed in a social media post that he isn't "Israeli enough" to attend the June 14 event after being banned for his comments about Israel and Jeffrey Epstein, calling the upcoming spectacle "straight (Israel flag emoji) slop".

In a lengthy video uploaded to his Instagram account, Strickland also revealed that he still plans to travel to Washington, DC, to protest the event and voice his displeasure with the Trump administration.

On Sunday, the UFC icon provided an update on the saga, revealing that he had spoken with UFC Chief Business Officer Hunter Campbell before taking another swipe at the Trump administration.

"I talked to Hunter yesterday about the White House ban and what I said. He just laughed and we carried on," Strickland posted on X. "Regardless of the administration's fascist views on speech, the UFC is holding the line for the 1st amendment..."

Replying to his tweet, one fan questioned whether Strickland was now going to the event given his positive conversation with Campbell, but "Tarzan" confirmed this was not the case, though he did confirm he will still be in the capital on the day.

"I will be in DC. Isn't there a fan greet? Maybe I'll go there," Strickland responded, referring to the UFC Freedom 250 Fan Fest due to take place on The Ellipse over the weekend.

Given Strickland's reputation for being one of the most outspoken fighters in UFC history, it is likely that he will still have plenty more to say about UFC Freedom 250 and the Trump administration in the lead-up to the event.

In his Instagram post last week, however, Strickland made clear that whatever protest he participates in will be a "peaceful" one, not wanting to cause any unwanted trouble.

"Apparently, I'm not American enough to go to Freedom 250, but I still got my ticket," he said. "So, maybe we'll just go, I'll bring the belt, and we'll just stand outside the gate and we'll just let 'em know what we really think about Trump and Israel, you know?"

Strickland said he has spoken with UFC Chief Business Officer Hunter Campbell

He then added in a separate clip: "You guys, I already bought my plane ticket. We're f---ing going. I'm gonna bring the belt, I'm gonna get a big f---ing bull horn and we're gonna go right up to the gates.

"So, if you guys are going to be there, let's f---ing go. Not in a threatening way, we're gonna do a peaceful protest."

Elsewhere, a federal lawsuit is seeking to put the brakes on the planned UFC fight card on the White House South Lawn, claiming that the Trump administration's approval of the June 14 event was unlawful.
